Assertion routes juan's "austria" label (1851-1917, 1042 rows) to AUT-1800-1918 "Austria (Cisleithania)" (300,560 km², wiki_status=draft). The draft wiki already flags the classic union-scope risk (Austria vs Austria-Hungary) and claims a wheat-area cross-check against Cisleithania, but per the skepticism rule I verified independently rather than trusting the draft. I pulled the raw juan rows from /home/usuario/Nextcloud/whep/layer_b/consolidated_layer_b.parquet for iso3c=aut, item=wheat, across the full observed span. Wheat production/area rise smoothly and gradually from 1851 (740k t) through a WWI-era dip, peaking at 1.9M t in 1912, then collapses catastrophically to ~140k t/150k ha in 1919 — the latter break lines up exactly with the truncated post-Saint-Germain Austrian Republic (successor AUT-1918-1919/1919-2025), confirming the 1918/1919 boundary is real and correctly split off. Critically, there is NO discontinuity around 1859 (loss of Lombardy), 1866 (loss of Venetia) or 1867 (Ausgleich/dual-monarchy constitutional change) — if the source's "Austria" had included Lombardy-Venetia before their loss, we would expect a step-down in the early 1860s; instead values in 1851-1859 are LOWER than the 1870s, consistent with ordinary agricultural intensification in a constant territory, not a shrinking one. This independently corroborates the wiki's claim that the Ausgleich was constitutional, not territorial, and that the source already reports on Cisleithanian-crownland boundaries from 1851 onward, never the whole Habsburg Empire or Lombardy-Venetia. Territory is therefore both equal to the candidate and constant across the whole 1851-1917 span, supporting verified_equal.

review.basis: The assertion routes 1,003 rows of "hungary" (source juan, 1851-1917) to HUN-1800-1918 "Kingdom of Hungary (Transleithania)" (area 325,421 km²) via ISO match. The candidate's wiki page (draft status, so not leaned on alone) cites an external authority — Mitchell's International Historical Statistics — which defines pre-1918 "Hungary" in statistical series as Transleithania (Lands of the Holy Crown of St. Stephen: Hungary proper + Croatia-Slavonia + Transylvania + Vojvodina + Slovakia + Carpathian Ruthenia), not the post-Trianon rump. That is independent corroboration beyond the page's own say-so, since Mitchell is a recognized external compilation, not the prior agent's invention. Magnitude check: staple_magnitudes show wheat median 3,067,000 t, rye 1,185,000 t, maize 2,312,037 t (n≈102-103) — plausible for a ~20-million-population, 325,000 km² breadbasket region (historically "granary of Europe"), and far too large for post-Trianon Hungary (~93,000 km², modern-day scale ~5M t only with 20th-c. intensification) — consistent with the Transleithania scope, not the shrunken successor. The neighbor_segments show the very next period (1918-1919) is routed to HUN-1918-1919, the small post-Trianon successor, and the magnitude table (though not shown per-period) combined with the well-known ~71% territorial loss at Trianon implies an expected large step-down there — consistent with a real territorial break at 1918, not a routing artifact. However, I flag a residual vintage concern the page does not address: within the observed span itself (1851-1917), Hungary's administrative composition was not static — the Voivodeship of Serbia/Banat of Temeschwar was abolished into Hungary in 1860, Transylvania was merged in via the 1867 Ausgleich, and the Military Frontier was dissolved into Croatia-Slavonia only in 1881. Whether the source ("juan") reports a single retrofitted Transleithania definition throughout 1851-1917 (as Mitchell's IHS conventionally does for comparability) or reports actual year-specific administrative Hungary (which would be smaller before 1867) cannot be confirmed from the bundle alone. Given this uncertainty about whether the reporting territory was genuinely constant across the full 55-year span, best_available rather than verified_equal is the honest classification, even though the polity-level routing (Hungary=Transleithania, not Cisleithania-Austria and not post-Trianon Hungary) is correct.
review.wiki_note: Page cites Mitchell's IHS for the Transleithania definition but does not address that Hungary's own administrative composition shifted within the observed 1851-1917 span itself (Banat/Voivodina merged 1860, Transylvania merged 1867 via Ausgleich, Military Frontier dissolved into Croatia-Slavonia 1881) — worth noting whether the source's series is a retrofitted constant-territory series (Mitchell convention) or tracks actual year-specific borders, since that changes whether pre-1867 rows are strictly comparable to later ones under the same 325,421 km² envelope.

Since I cannot confirm from the bundle alone whether the "juan" source's Albania-labeled rows for 1941-1943 report on the enlarged wartime borders or continue reporting only the 1913 territory (statistical continuity through wartime disruption makes the latter plausible but not certain), and the span exceeds 30 years, I am not claiming the reporting territory was provably constant throughout. The routing to ALB-1913-2025 is still the correct and only sensible existing polity for this label across the whole span -- there is no separate WHEP polity for wartime Greater Albania and no evidence the data itself reflects an expanded territory -- so this is a confirm, but with confirm_kind best_available rather than verified_equal, given the unresolved possibility of a mid-span territorial change during the 1941-1943 occupation.
